title: Genting Highlands Food: Where to Eat, Top and Mid Hill
metaDescription: Genting Highlands food by where you are: SkyAvenue floors, First World Plaza, Highlands Hotel, Sky Sentral at mid hill, Gohtong Jaya and Genting Permai.

contentBlocks.content: Genting Highlands food is spread over the whole mountain, so the easy way to choose is by where you are standing. At the top, most restaurants sit on Level 1 and Level 4 of SkyAvenue, with more in First World Plaza and the hotels around it. At mid hill, Sky Sentral, where the Awana SkyWay starts, has food outlets of its own. Lower down, Gohtong Jaya and Genting Permai have local restaurants off the resort roads. Each place below links to its Google Maps listing, with the lot number it gives, so you can walk straight there. Coming from the airport? A direct bus runs from KLIA2 to Awana Genting Highland, and you book it on ttklia.com.
Key Takeaways
Where are most of the restaurants? On Level 1 and Level 4 of SkyAvenue, at the top. The mall's directory gives the level and lot of each one.
Is there hawker food at the top? Yes. Malaysian Food Street on Level 4 of SkyAvenue brings 20 hawkers from around Malaysia under one roof, open daily 8am to 10pm.
Can I eat halal? Rimba Resto in First World Plaza says every dish is halal. Anywhere else, look for the JAKIM halal certificate at the counter before you order.
Can I eat before I ride up? Yes. Sky Sentral at mid hill has food outlets, including Home Noodle on Level 2 of the Awana SkyWay station.
How do I get here from KLIA2? Take the direct bus from the KLIA2 Transportation Hub, Level 1, to Awana Genting Highland. Book it on ttklia.com.
SkyAvenue, Level 1

SkyAvenue is the mall at the top. The Awana SkyWay arrives at Genting Highlands Station on its Level 4 (Resorts World Genting). The mall opens daily from 10am, and its directory lists every restaurant with its level and lot number (Resorts World Genting, SkyAvenue). Level 1 has the longest row of them.

Madam Kwan's is at Lot SA-T2-30, Level 1. Google Maps lists it as a Malay restaurant, and the brand describes its food as Malaysian, cooked from traditional recipes (Madam Kwan's). It has a second outlet at mid hill, covered below.

Burger & Lobster Genting is at Lot SA-T2-13, Level 1. Resorts World Genting says its lobsters are imported from Nova Scotia, Canada, and its burger uses halal-grade beef from Stanbroke, Australia. As listed on 5 Nov 2026, it opens 12nn to 10pm Monday to Thursday, 12nn to 11pm on Friday, 11am to 11pm on Saturday and 11am to 10pm on Sunday (Resorts World Genting, Burger & Lobster).

LeNu Chef Wai's Noodle Bar is at Lot T2-03, Level 1. The SkyAvenue directory puts it in one unit with Paradise Dynasty and Canton Paradise (Resorts World Genting). Walk the floor once, then match the lot number on the shop front to the one here.
SkyAvenue, Level 4 and Level 5

Level 4 is where you step off the cable car. Malaysian Food Street, Lot T2C-MFS, is Resorts World Genting's own hawker hall (Resorts World Genting). It gathers 20 hawkers from places such as KL Chinatown, Penang, Melaka, Ipoh and Kuching, and opens daily from 8am to 10pm. Its dish list includes chicken rice, curry laksa, char kway teow, pork congee and bak kut teh, so the hall is not pork free (Resorts World Genting, Malaysian Food Street).

SOULed OUT is at Lot T2C-06, Level 4. Its website describes Western and Asian dishes, lists wines and spirits on its drinks menu, and gives its hours as 12pm to 12am daily (SOULed OUT). You reserve through the WhatsApp link on that page.
Harry Ramsden's is at Lot T2C-22-23A, Level 4 (Resorts World Genting). Google Maps describes it as a branch of the long-standing fish and chip chain, with takeaway and table service.

One floor up, Beauty In The Pot takes Lots T3-25 to T3-30 on Level 5 (Resorts World Genting). Google Maps lists it as a hot pot restaurant, and Paradise Group publishes a separate menu for the SkyAvenue Genting Highlands outlet (Paradise Group). Eat on Level 4 or 5 before you ride down, so you are not hungry in the gondola queue.
First World Plaza and First World Hotel

First World Hotel sits in the middle of the resort, with First World Plaza and SkyAvenue next to it (Resorts World Genting, First World Hotel). Rimba Resto is at Lot T2A-20, Level 2, First World Plaza. Its website describes food from the Nusantara region, Thailand and Malaysia, and says every dish is halal (Rimba Resto). Its partnership page calls it a halal certified restaurant (Rimba Resto). The JAKIM directory searches by company name, and we could not match it there, so ask to see the certificate at the counter.
Steam Era Genting Seafood Restaurant (蒸时代 云顶) is listed on Google Maps as a steamboat restaurant at Lot FW-T2-02. Open the pin for walking directions inside the resort before you set off.
Highlands Hotel

Tai Fook Hong Kong Daipaidong (大福香港大排档) is listed on Google Maps as a restaurant at Lot R/L1.3, Highlands Hotel. A dai pai dong is the Cantonese name for a street food stall. Resorts World Genting has renamed its hotels: the former Resort Hotel is now called Highlands Hotel, and the former Highlands Hotel is now RW Hotel (Resorts World Genting, Highlands Hotel). Follow the Google Maps pin, not an old sign.
Sky Sentral and the Awana SkyWay station, mid hill

Sky Sentral is the mid hill terminal where the express buses stop and the Awana SkyWay starts. Resorts World Genting describes it as a bus station, a cable car station and outlets, next to Genting Highlands Premium Outlets, and confirms it has food and beverage outlets (Resorts World Genting, Sky Sentral). The cable car boards on Level 4, runs from 7AM to 11PM and takes about 10 minutes to the top (Resorts World Genting, Awana SkyWay).
Home Noodle Genting Highlands is listed on Google Maps at Lot 2-11, Level 2, Awana Skyway Station. It suits a bowl while you wait for the bus back to KL or KLIA2.

In the outlets next door, Madam Kwan's lists Madam Kwan's Select (GHPO) at Suite 1518, Low Street (Madam Kwan's). Leave a big case at the baggage counter on Level 2 of Sky Sentral before you shop (Resorts World Genting).
Gohtong Jaya and Genting Permai, further down

Gohtong Jaya is lower down the mountain, where the second cable car, the Genting SkyWay, starts at Gohtong Sentral Station. It runs 3.4 km to Resorts World Station at the peak in about 15 minutes, from 9AM to 7PM (Resorts World Genting, Genting SkyWay). Lamei Hotpot Gohtong Jaya (辣妹火锅 云顶半山) is at 12, Persiaran Jati 3A, listed on Google Maps as a Chinese restaurant.

Makanan Enak Genting Permai is at No 7, Jalan Boulevard 2, Genting Permai, listed on Google Maps as a restaurant. The bus from KLIA2 stops at Sky Sentral, so plan both of these as a stop on a drive up with a car and driver.
Eating halal in Genting

Halal and non-halal kitchens sit close together here. A Google Maps category or a sign on the door is the business's own label, not certification. Look for the JAKIM halal certificate at the counter, or search the Halal Malaysia directory before you go. Remember that Malaysian Food Street lists pork dishes. The SkyAvenue prayer room is on Level G, near the cinema (Resorts World Genting).
Getting to Genting from KLIA2

From KLIA2, take the direct bus from the KLIA2 Transportation Hub, Level 1, to Awana Genting Highland at Sky Sentral. Aerobus and Resorts World Tour run it, and the fare, with the terminal fee included, is shown on the booking page (ttklia.com). Our KLIA2 bus station guide walks you from arrivals to the bus.

Already in KL? Read KL to Genting Highlands for every way up. For a day with your own driver and a stop in Gohtong Jaya, book an 8 or 10 hour car charter on ttklia.com, and plan the stops with our Genting Highlands day trip guide. Between meals, see things to do in Genting.

contentBlocks.content: Frequently Asked Questions
Where can I eat in Genting Highlands?
You can eat in Genting Highlands at SkyAvenue at the top, mostly on Level 1 and Level 4, in First World Plaza, at Sky Sentral at mid hill, and in Gohtong Jaya and Genting Permai further down.
Is there halal food in Genting Highlands?

Yes, there is halal food in Genting Highlands. Rimba Resto, Level 2, First World Plaza, says every dish is halal. Elsewhere, look for the JAKIM halal certificate at the counter, because a halal sign or a Google Maps label is the shop's own claim.
Where is Malaysian Food Street in Genting?
Malaysian Food Street is on Level 4 of SkyAvenue, Lot T2C-MFS, on the floor where the Awana SkyWay arrives. It opens daily from 8am to 10pm, as listed on 5 Nov 2026.
Can I eat at Sky Sentral before taking the cable car?
Yes, Sky Sentral has food and beverage outlets. Home Noodle is listed at Lot 2-11, Level 2, Awana Skyway Station, and the cable car boards on Level 4.
How do I get to Genting Highlands from KLIA2?
Take the direct bus from the KLIA2 Transportation Hub, Level 1, to Awana Genting Highland. Aerobus and Resorts World Tour run it. Book on ttklia.com, where the fare is shown for your date.
Conclusion

Genting Highlands food is easiest to plan by floor and by station. Eat on Level 1 or Level 4 of SkyAvenue at the top, try First World Plaza for halal, grab noodles at Sky Sentral before the ride, and save Gohtong Jaya and Genting Permai for a drive. Google Maps listings change, so open each link to check the opening hours on the day you go. Book your bus from KLIA2 to Genting on ttklia.com.
